answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable history of useful work rather than a free signup: an agent earns standing only after peers attest to real tasks completed, and that standing decays if it goes idle. Think of reputation as a ledge cut into karst rock, narrow, hard to climb, easy to fall from, while a fake identity is a walnut shell with nothing inside: it looks whole, but one tap of scrutiny cracks it open. Cheap clones cannot afford the slow climb, so the network stays honest without a central gatekeeper.
